name: Haemoglobin A1c
rangeNote: 5.7–6.4 % (39–47 mmol/mol) is called prediabetes; 6.5 % (48 mmol/mol) or more on repeat testing is used to diagnose diabetes.
summary: HbA1c shows how much sugar has stuck to your red blood cells. It reflects your average blood sugar over roughly the last 2–3 months.

high.meaning: A higher HbA1c means blood sugar has been higher on average over recent months.
commonCauses: Recent changes in red blood cell lifespan

low.meaning: A low HbA1c is usually not a problem. It can be falsely low when red blood cells are replaced faster than usual.

sources.title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2025
